import pandas as pd

# Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the first numerical index column
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_3/training_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_3/training_1.csv"
source2_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_3/training_2.csv"

df_source0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)
df_source1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)
df_source2 = pd.read_csv(source2_path, index_col=0)

# Operation History:
# 1) JOIN : [["Source3_3_2", "Source3_3_1"], ["movie_id", "movie_id"]]
# 2) JOIN : [["Source3_3_0", "Source3_3_2"], ["user_id", "user_id"]]

# Step 1: Join Source3_3_2 and Source3_3_1 on movie_id
df_join_2_1 = pd.merge(df_source2, df_source1[['movie_id', 'title']], on='movie_id', how='inner')

# Step 2: Join Source3_3_0 and the result of previous join on user_id
df_join_all = pd.merge(df_source0, df_join_2_1, on='user_id', how='inner')

# Now, select and convert columns to match the target schema:
# Target Schema: ['title': string, 'user_id': float, 'age': float, 'occupation': float, 'movie_id': integer, 'rating': float, 'timestamp': float]

# Convert types accordingly:
df_result = pd.DataFrame()

# title: string (already string)
df_result['title'] = df_join_all['title'].astype(str)

# user_id: float
df_result['user_id'] = df_join_all['user_id'].astype(float)

# age: float
df_result['age'] = df_join_all['age'].astype(float)

# occupation: float
df_result['occupation'] = df_join_all['occupation'].astype(float)

# movie_id: integer
df_result['movie_id'] = df_join_all['movie_id'].astype(int)

# rating: float
df_result['rating'] = df_join_all['rating'].astype(float)

# timestamp: float
df_result['timestamp'] = df_join_all['timestamp'].astype(float)

# Write the result to the target path
target_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_3/target_multisource.csv"
df_result.to_csv(target_path, index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the first numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_3/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_3/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_3/training_2.csv", index_col=0)

# Join Source3_3_2 and Source3_3_1 on movie_id
joined_0 = pd.merge(source2, source1, on="movie_id", how="inner")

# Join Source3_3_0 and the above join on user_id
joined_1 = pd.merge(source0, joined_0, on="user_id", how="inner")

# Group by the leftmost non-float columns in target schema that are unique identifiers:
# title (string), user_id (float but used as id), age (float), occupation (float), movie_id (int)
# Aggregate rating and timestamp by mean to match target averages
result = joined_1.groupby(
    ["title", "user_id", "age", "occupation", "movie_id"], as_index=False
).agg(
    rating=("rating", "mean"),
    timestamp=("timestamp", "mean")
)

# Reorder columns to match target schema exactly
result = result[["title", "user_id", "age", "occupation", "movie_id", "rating", "timestamp"]]

# Write to output CSV
result.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_3/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
